title: No sound from HDMI/DisplayPort monitor or TV, or it is missing from the output list
symptoms: Picture shows on the monitor or TV but no sound comes from it
The monitor or TV (NVIDIA/AMD High Definition Audio or Intel Display Audio) is not listed under Sound > Output
The HDMI device shows as Disabled or Not plugged in in the Sound control panel
causes: Windows is sending sound to a different default output device
The HDMI/DisplayPort audio endpoint is disabled or hidden
The monitor has no speakers, or its own volume or input is muted
The graphics card's display audio device was not detected or its driver is missing or outdated

signals: A display is connected over HDMI or DisplayPort but no audio endpoint from NVIDIA High Definition Audio, AMD High Definition Audio or Intel Display Audio is active
A display audio endpoint exists but is in Disabled or Unplugged state
The default render endpoint is not the display audio endpoint the user expects
No display audio device appears under Sound, video and game controllers in Device Manager

fixes.title: Select the monitor or TV as the output device
steps: On Windows 11, open Settings > System > Sound and choose the monitor or TV under Output.
On Windows 10, open Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Sound, right-click the monitor or TV on the Playback tab and choose Set as Default Device.
Make sure the volume is not at zero.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: set a USB or HDMI audio device as the default output
Samsung official troubleshooting page for no sound from HDMI device, step 1
Two later replies confirm 'Setting to default worked for me'

fixes.title: Check that the monitor or TV has speakers and is not muted
steps: Check that the monitor or TV has built-in speakers and supports audio over HDMI or DisplayPort.
Turn up the volume and turn off mute using the monitor's or TV's own buttons or remote.
If the monitor has no speakers, choose your speakers or headphones as the output device instead.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: an external monitor without speakers set as default gives no audio
Samsung official page notes some monitors have no speakers or do not support HDMI audio

fixes.title: Show and enable a disabled HDMI/DisplayPort audio device
steps: Open Settings > System > Sound and select More sound settings (Windows 11) or Sound Control Panel (Windows 10).
On the Playback tab, right-click an empty area and check Show Disabled Devices and Show Disconnected Devices.
If the monitor or TV appears greyed out, right-click it and choose Enable.
Right-click it again and choose Set as Default Device.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: check the device is enabled (Use this device / Disable checkbox)
Samsung official page step 3: show disconnected devices and enable the HDMI device

fixes.title: Make Windows detect the display audio device again
steps: Open Device Manager.
Select Sound, video and game controllers, then choose Action > Scan for hardware changes.
Check that NVIDIA High Definition Audio, AMD High Definition Audio or Intel Display Audio now appears.
Set the monitor or TV as the default output device.

sources.signal: Post marked as the thread Solution; poster confirms the TV then played sound
Microsoft Tech Community thread; user reports Scan for hardware changes brings the monitor audio back

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the graphics driver that provides HDMI/DisplayPort audio
steps: Run Windows Update and install any display or audio driver updates.
Download the current driver for your graphics card from NVIDIA, AMD, Intel or your PC maker.
Run the installer and make sure the HD Audio driver component is included.
Restart the PC with the monitor or TV turned on and connected.
If sound stopped after a driver update, open Device Manager, right-click the display audio device, choose Properties > Driver > Roll Back Driver instead.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: update, reinstall or roll back the audio driver; check the manufacturer's site
Samsung official page step 5: get HDMI audio drivers from the graphics card maker (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel)
Microsoft Q&A advisor answer (not marked accepted): missing display audio means a graphics audio driver problem; clean-install the graphics driver

title: Monitor or TV sound stops after the display sleeps or is turned off
symptoms: Sound from the monitor or TV stops after the screen turns off and back on
The monitor or TV disappears from the output list after the display sleeps
Sound switches to another device after the display wakes up
Restarting the PC brings the sound back
causes: When the display turns off, Windows treats its HDMI/DisplayPort audio as unavailable and switches to another output
The display audio device is not detected again when the display wakes
Graphics or display audio driver problems with power events

signals: A display audio endpoint was the default before display sleep and is now Unplugged, Not present, or no longer the default
The display audio PnP device is missing after a display power-off event while the display is connected

fixes.title: Select the monitor or TV as the output again
steps: Make sure the monitor or TV is turned on.
Open Settings > System > Sound and choose the monitor or TV under Output.
If it is not listed, try the next fix.

sources.signal: Microsoft Tech Community thread; users report Windows switches to another output when displays sleep
Official Microsoft page: choose the HDMI device as the default output

fixes.title: Make Windows detect the display audio device again
steps: Make sure the monitor or TV is turned on.
Open Device Manager and choose Action > Scan for hardware changes.
Select the monitor or TV under Settings > System > Sound > Output.

sources.signal: User reports Scan for hardware changes restores monitor audio after idle; described as a temporary fix
Post marked as the thread Solution: scan for hardware changes revealed NVIDIA High Definition Audio and the TV

fixes.title: Update the graphics and display audio driver
steps: Download the current driver for your graphics card from NVIDIA, AMD, Intel or your PC maker.
Install it, including the HD Audio component, and restart the PC with the display on.
Test whether sound survives the display turning off and on again.

sources.signal: User reports 'Now its working' after updating NVIDIA graphics and audio drivers
Official Microsoft page: update the audio driver or get it from the manufacturer

title: USB headset, DAC or microphone cuts out, disconnects or is not detected
symptoms: USB headset or microphone stops working after a few minutes of silence
USB DAC or audio interface disconnects and reconnects at random
USB audio device is not recognized after the PC wakes from sleep until a restart
Sound cuts out when the device is plugged into a USB hub
causes: USB selective suspend lets Windows power down the USB port to save power
Power management on the USB Root Hub turns off the hub the device is connected to
USB hubs or extenders that cannot supply enough power or interfere with the connection

signals: The active power plan has USB selective suspend enabled
USB Root Hub devices allow the computer to turn them off to save power
A USB audio endpoint repeatedly changes between present and not present
The USB audio device is connected through a hub rather than directly to the PC

fixes.title: Plug the device directly into a different USB port
steps: Unplug the USB headset, DAC or microphone from any hub, extender or front-panel port.
Plug it directly into a USB port on the PC (on a desktop, a rear port on the motherboard).
Select it under Settings > System > Sound and test again.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: try a different USB port for USB speakers or headphones
Rational Acoustics official support: avoid USB extenders and multi-port hubs for audio interfaces

fixes.title: Turn off USB selective suspend
steps: Open Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Power Options.
Select Change plan settings for the active plan, then Change advanced power settings.
Expand USB settings > USB selective suspend setting.
Set it to Disabled. On a laptop, set both On battery and Plugged in.
Select Apply, then OK.
fixes.command: powercfg /setacvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT 2a737441-1930-4402-8d77-b2bebba308a3 48e6b7a6-50f5-4782-a5d4-53bb8f07e226 0; powercfg /setdcvalueindex SCHEME_CURRENT 2a737441-1930-4402-8d77-b2bebba308a3 48e6b7a6-50f5-4782-a5d4-53bb8f07e226 0; powercfg /setactive SCHEME_CURRENT

sources.signal: Logitech official support: devices such as headsets stop responding; disable USB selective suspend
M-Audio official support: USB device disconnects randomly; disable USB selective suspend
Puget Systems support article (2018): random USB disconnects and devices not waking from sleep

fixes.title: Stop Windows from turning off USB Root Hubs to save power
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Universal Serial Bus controllers.
Right-click USB Root Hub and choose Properties.
On the Power Management tab, clear Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power, then select OK.
Repeat for every USB Root Hub, or use View > Devices by connection to find the hub and host controller above the audio device.
Restart the PC.

sources.signal: Logitech official support: uncheck the USB Root Hub power-saving option
Rational Acoustics official support: audio device disconnects after inactivity; disable root hub and host controller power saving
Puget Systems support article: disable power management on all root hubs if problems persist
